The 2005 romantic comedy Monster-in-Law marked Jane Fonda’s grand return to the screen after a 15-year retirement. Fonda shared that she based her outrageous, overbearing character, Viola Fields, on her own ex-husband, Ted Turner. The only doctored photo on that table was a Time magazine cover featuring Fonda. She was originally scheduled for the real cover, but Pope John Paul II passed away in April 2005 and took the headline spot.  Fonda admitted the movie's screenplay wasn’t great, but she chose it for her comeback because she knew working alongside Jennifer Lopez would guarantee a massive audience.

Despite mixed reviews from critics, the movie was a box office hit, grossing over $155 million worldwide against a $43 million budget.

source_details.synopsis: Monster-in-Law is a 2005 romantic comedy film directed by Robert Luketic, written by Anya Kochoff and starring Jennifer Lopez, Jane Fonda, Michael Vartan, and Wanda Sykes. It marked a return to cinema for Fonda, being her first film in 15 years since Stanley & Iris in 1990. Temp Charlotte Cantillini's love life has been stagnant for ages--until she repeatedly cross paths with Dr. Kevin Fields and they instantly connect. Soon, their relationship advances so she meets his controlling mother Violet, who goes to great lengths to separate them.
